$comment: Generated by node contract/tools/generate.mjs. Edit contract/tools, not these files.
notes: input.text is the document as a client reads it; it is checked as UTF-8 bytes. errors and warnings are sorted, unique codes from section 9.7. Warnings are only reported for a document without errors.

Order: section 12 first, where a refused text is the error schema under every intake and keep is false; then a repeated member name on the canonical text, reported alone; then, for local intake, the identity; then the schema and the rules.
keep is valid for peer and local intake. For applied intake it is true unless section 12 refuses the text.

assignsIdentity is true for local intake when the document has no controller block or a block whose id is absent or null; the document is then checked with a fresh setup id, revision 1 and an empty lineage.
Cases tagged agent-enforced are refused by agent 3.1.0 on config set as well. The base document is the tower setup with setup id setup-3f9c2a71-8d04-4e6b-9a53-7c21b0e5d846.

documents.name: duplicate-member
documents.purpose: A system that writes agent twice. Parsers disagree about which copy counts, so the document means different things on different devices; this is checked first, on the text, and no other rule is reported.

documents.name: duplicate-machine
documents.purpose: Two machines share the id tower, so a route, a record and a binding naming it are ambiguous.

documents.name: duplicate-site
documents.purpose: Two sites share the id home.

documents.name: duplicate-system
documents.purpose: Two systems of one machine share the id linux.

documents.name: duplicate-endpoint
documents.purpose: Two endpoints of one machine share the id lan, so a remembered route is ambiguous.

documents.name: unknown-site
documents.purpose: A machine names a site that sites[] does not define (fixture controller-document.invalid-unknown-site.json).

documents.name: helper-self
documents.purpose: A machine is its own wake helper (fixture controller-document.invalid-self-helper.json).

documents.name: helper-unknown
documents.purpose: A wake helper names a machine the setup does not have.

documents.name: helper-alias
documents.purpose: wake.helper names nas and wake.helpers[0] names pi, so a 1.2 client and a 1.4 client try different machines (fixture controller-document.invalid-helper-mismatch.json).

documents.name: helper-cycle
documents.purpose: Two machines wake each other, so each waits for the other to be awake first (fixture controller-document.invalid-helper-cycle.json).

documents.name: helper-cycle-through-alias
documents.purpose: The same ring written only with the singular helper key, as a 1.2 editor writes it. The alias is a helper too.

documents.name: helper-self-beside-empty-helpers
documents.purpose: The alias beside an empty helpers list still names a helper, because a 1.2 client runs it. Reading helpers ?? [helper] skips it and stores a document every client refuses.

documents.name: schema-version-2
documents.purpose: version stays 1: a bump would make every 1.2 client refuse documents for keys it can ignore.

documents.name: schema-version-missing
documents.purpose: A document without version is refused; section 12 already refuses it before any rule is read.

documents.name: schema-51-machines
documents.purpose: At most 50 machines.

documents.name: schema-21-endpoints
documents.purpose: At most 20 endpoints on a machine.

documents.name: schema-11-systems
documents.purpose: At most 10 systems on a machine.

documents.name: schema-21-sites
documents.purpose: At most 20 sites in one setup.

documents.name: schema-6-helpers
documents.purpose: At most 5 wake helpers.

documents.name: schema-empty-lan-prefixes
documents.purpose: lanPrefixes, when present, has at least one entry; editors omit it instead of writing an empty list.

documents.name: schema-port-0
documents.purpose: Port 0 is not a port.

documents.name: schema-port-65536
documents.purpose: One over the highest port.

documents.name: schema-port-string
documents.purpose: A port is a JSON integer, never a string.

documents.name: schema-bad-mac
documents.purpose: A MAC address has six groups.

documents.name: schema-source-android
documents.purpose: source is the kind of client (mac, desktop, phone, cli, legacy), not a platform name; the device name goes in device.

documents.name: schema-setup-id-65
documents.purpose: A setup id is at most 64 characters.

documents.name: schema-setup-id-at
documents.purpose: An @ is in the generic token grammar and not in a setup id, which the agent refuses with bad-argument (C10).

documents.name: schema-helper-action-colon
documents.purpose: A wake action is a configured id, which has no colon.

documents.name: schema-lineage-33
documents.purpose: A lineage holds at most 32 hashes.

documents.name: schema-lineage-duplicate
documents.purpose: A document cannot descend from one ancestor twice.

documents.name: schema-lineage-uppercase
documents.purpose: Lineage hashes are lowercase hex, the form every client computes.

documents.name: schema-bad-repo
documents.purpose: A repository is owner/name.

documents.name: schema-controller-without-revision
documents.purpose: A controller block has an id and a revision.

documents.name: schema-machine-without-id
documents.purpose: Every machine has an id.

documents.name: warn-no-machines
documents.purpose: A setup with no machines yet is a setup: it is how one starts.

documents.name: warn-machine-no-systems
documents.purpose: A machine with no systems yet is accepted and not driven; Android used to refuse the whole setup for it (C3).

documents.name: warn-machine-no-endpoints
documents.purpose: A machine nobody can reach yet is accepted.

documents.name: warn-system-no-agent
documents.purpose: A system without an agent command is not driven, and that is a warning.

documents.name: warn-endpoint-no-id
documents.purpose: An endpoint without an id cannot be remembered as a route; it is still used.

documents.name: warn-endpoint-no-user
documents.purpose: An endpoint without a user logs in as whatever the device's own ssh configuration says.

documents.name: warn-endpoint-unknown-system
documents.purpose: An endpoint hint naming a system the machine does not have is ignored, not refused.

documents.name: host-all-digits-undialable
documents.purpose: A host of digits passes the document guard but is an integer address to a resolver; the entry is skipped, never dialled.

documents.name: host-trailing-dot-undialable
documents.purpose: A trailing dot passes the guard and fails the dial grammar.

documents.name: legacy-ssh-host-undialable
documents.purpose: The deprecated machine.ssh host is held to the dial grammar too; with it the machine has a host, so it is not missing endpoints.

documents.name: warn-wake-no-mac
documents.purpose: A wake block with helpers and no MAC: helpers still work, direct wake does not.

documents.name: warn-wake-no-mac-at-site
documents.purpose: A wake block at a site with no broadcast anywhere, and no MAC address: nothing is woken directly, so no broadcast is defaulted either.

documents.name: warn-wake-unplaced
documents.purpose: A MAC address with no site, no lanPrefix and no helper: no client can tell when it is on the machine's network.

documents.name: warn-wake-lan-prefix-invalid
documents.purpose: A wake.lanPrefix that is a full address never matches, so it places nothing: the block is as unplaced as one without lanPrefix.

documents.name: warn-wake-broadcast-defaulted
documents.purpose: A machine that can be woken directly with no broadcast address: clients derive one, which Android used to refuse outright.

documents.name: warn-helper-alias-unused
documents.purpose: wake.helper beside an empty wake.helpers: clients disagree about whether it counts.

documents.name: warn-helper-other-site
documents.purpose: A helper at another site works only if its action reaches the target's network some other way.

documents.name: warn-helper-not-always-on
documents.purpose: A helper not marked alwaysOn may itself need waking first.

documents.name: warn-shared-prefix
documents.purpose: Two sites whose prefixes overlap: matching one does not say which site a device is on. The prefixes are compared parsed, not as text.

documents.name: warn-prefix-invalid
documents.purpose: A full address is not a prefix: it never matches, and the setup is not refused for it.

documents.name: warn-prefix-without-dot
documents.purpose: Without the trailing dot, a client that predates section 10.1 also matches 192.168.10.x.

documents.name: warn-broadcast-invalid
documents.purpose: A broadcast entry that is a name is skipped and never resolved.

documents.name: system-empty-agent
documents.purpose: An empty agent is the same as none: the system is not driven, and the document is valid.

documents.name: partial-machines
documents.purpose: A setup half way through being written, with every gap Android used to refuse: no systems, no endpoints, an endpoint without id or user, a hint to a system that does not exist, a wake block without broadcast. All warnings, no errors (C3).

documents.name: site-named-without-sites
documents.purpose: A site name is only checked against a sites list that has entries; a setup without sites places nobody.

documents.name: endpoints-without-ids-are-not-duplicates
documents.purpose: Two endpoints without an id are never duplicates of each other; the desktop counted them as such.

documents.name: canonical-bytes-first
documents.purpose: A byte order mark, CRLF line endings and trailing blank lines: acceptance reads the canonical bytes, so none of it matters.

documents.name: local-without-controller
documents.purpose: A pasted document with no controller block gets a fresh setup id, revision 1 and an empty lineage before it is checked.

documents.name: local-controller-without-id
documents.purpose: A controller block without an id is given one too, keeping its other keys.

documents.name: local-controller-id-null
documents.purpose: An id of null is no id: an editor that clears the field writes null, and the document is given an identity rather than refused for it.

documents.name: local-identity-then-checked
documents.purpose: Local intake assigns the identity and then checks everything else: a pasted document with a duplicate machine is still refused.

documents.name: local-with-identity
documents.purpose: A local document that already has an id keeps it.

documents.name: peer-without-controller
documents.purpose: The text of local-without-controller read from a peer. A machine may hold a document without a controller block (a 2.x copy); under peer intake it is valid and nothing is assigned.

documents.name: peer-controller-without-id
documents.purpose: The text of local-controller-without-id read from a peer: a controller block without an id breaks the schema, because only local intake assigns one.

documents.name: host-comma-star
documents.purpose: A comma and a star make a known_hosts pattern that pins one key for every host (fixture controller-document.invalid-host.json).

documents.name: host-leading-dash
documents.purpose: A host that starts with a hyphen is an ssh option (fixture controller-document.invalid-host-option.json).

documents.name: user-option
documents.purpose: A user that starts with a hyphen is an ssh option too.

documents.name: user-substitution
documents.purpose: A command substitution in a user (fixture controller-document.invalid-user.json).

documents.name: agent-argv-empty-item
documents.purpose: An empty argv item vanishes or becomes an empty argument depending on the shell (fixture controller-document.invalid-agent-argv.json).

documents.name: agent-argv-bell-character
documents.purpose: A control character in an argv item (fixture controller-document.invalid-agent-control.json).

documents.name: agent-argv-del-character
documents.purpose: U+007F is a control character as well.

documents.name: agent-argv-4097-bytes
documents.purpose: 2049 characters but 4097 UTF-8 bytes: the argv-item limit is counted in bytes, which a schema cannot, so it is checked in code.

documents.name: repo-dotdot
documents.purpose: A repository named .. turns every client's update URL into a path out of the owner (fixture controller-document.invalid-repo.json).

documents.name: applied-legacy-host-comma
documents.purpose: The document this device already applies, written before the guards existed, with a pattern in the deprecated ssh host. It is kept and shown with its error; that machine is disabled, and publishing is held until it is fixed.

documents.name: applied-version-2
documents.purpose: An applied document that breaks the schema is still kept, because section 12 accepts its bytes.

documents.name: applied-duplicate-member
documents.purpose: An applied document with a repeated member name is kept and shown with its error.

documents.name: applied-not-json
documents.purpose: Text that section 12 refuses is not a document at all: even applied intake cannot keep it.

input.text: this was a setup file once

documents.name: applied-valid
documents.purpose: A valid applied document, as a client reads it at start.
